messages:
maria: quick note — saw a weird routing gap this morning when tenant caps hit. primary model returned 503 and the request fell back, but header-affinity was lost and we returned a cold backup instance instead of the warm standby. impact: higher p95 for a handful of customers.
kevin: ugh, do we know which rule dropped the header? sounds like the gateway strip + rewrite path again.
olga: saw the logs — the header we use for tenant-affinity is `x-rd-affinity`. gateway was rewriting `x-rd-route` in the health-check proxy and we accidentally dropped the `affinity` header in the proxy forward.
sam: can you paste the minimal trace?
maria: sure — snippet from the proxy trace: ```
> incoming: x-rd-affinity: tenant-42; x-rd-route: primary
> proxy-rewrite: set x-rd-route: primary-v2
> forwarded: x-rd-route: primary-v2
```
kevin: so the probe path removed the other header when applying the `set` op. gateway rule engine is non-idempotent for header ops right now.
olga: correct. current rule semantics: `set` replaces header entirely, `append` keeps existing values. we used `set` to normalize routes.
lina: related: fallback selection currently prefers lowest-cost compatible model lane, not affinity. so even if affinity is present, we still pick a different model if it's cheaper. that's intended but combined with dropped header we get a cold model.
andy: proposal: introduce a `sticky` flag on route rules that preserves `x-rd-affinity` across proxies and forces fallback to use the affinity tag to pick standby models if available. also fall back to cost only if no affinity match.
kevin: +1 for sticky. implementation question: do we change gateway engine semantics (make `set` not drop unrelated headers) or teach rules to `preserve`? the former is safer long-term.
olga: changing global `set` semantics could be risky; lots of rules rely on replacing values. better to add an explicit `preserve_headers: ["x-rd-affinity"]` opt-in on route entries.
maria: operationally we need two things: 1) short-term patch to stop dropping affinity (either preserve global list or a hotfix in the proxy that forwards all `x-rd-*` by default), 2) longer term sticky route and fallback policy change so standby models are chosen if affinity present.
deploy-bot: deploy started: proxy-hotfix/2026-03-18T09:42Z — rolling to prod canaries (10%)
sam: for the fallback selection logic change, we should update the Console UX to show when affinity was respected vs ignored. add a telemetry flag `fallback_affinity_hit` so ops can measure regressions.
lina: agree. also add a metric `fallback_cold_start_rate` per tenant-model-lane. that will let Optimize suggest warm standbys for high-traffic tenants.
kevin: quasi-implementation sketch: ```
route {
  match: path /v1/generate
  route_key: tenant_header(x-rd-tenant)
  preserve_headers: ["x-rd-affinity"]
  fallback_policy: {
    prefer: ["affinity_match", "cost_optimal"]
    circuit_breaker: {
      error_pct: 10
      window_ms: 10000
    }
  }
}
```
olga: circuit-breaker triggers also need to bubble telemetry to the Console rollouts page, otherwise SRE can't correlate canary drops and fallback picks. add `cb_triggered` event with tags `{route, tenant, model_lane}`.
maria: action items: olga will patch proxy forward to preserve `x-rd-*` headers by default (hotfix). kevin + lina will spec `sticky` fallback policy + telemetry. sam will add Console telemetry widgets (fallback_affinity_hit, fallback_cold_start_rate, cb_triggered). andy will schedule a short post-deploy soak and metric dashboard.
andy: I'll book the soak and add a runbook note: if `fallback_affinity_hit` < 95% for any tenant after hotfix, roll back and investigate.
kevin: small UX note — Console should surface the exact header precedence for each route (show effective `preserve_headers` and `set/append` ops) so platform owners can debug these conflicts.
lina: will add to spec. also add a lint rule in repo that flags `set` on `x-rd-*` headers unless `preserve_headers` is explicit.
maria: thanks folks. expected timeline: hotfix in canary now, full roll after 1h soak, longer policy change next sprint. ping me if regressions. :thumbsup:
deploy-bot: deploy success: proxy-hotfix/2026-03-18T09:49Z — canary OK at 10%
sam: quick check — telemetry shows `x-rd-affinity` preserved in forwarded requests for the canary slice. cold-starts down ~72% in sample.
andy: great. leaving soak window open for 30m.
kevin: follow-up — let's discuss making fallback selection configurable per tenant (enterprise tenants could force affinity-only). low-priority but worth tracking.
maria: added to backlog. closing this thread after soak.
